finding.title: Buffer Overflow
finding.trigger: If int_type->name is longer than the buffer size allocated for it, a buffer overflow will occur.
finding.assumptions: The name of the constrained int type is obtained from user input or an external source and is not properly validated for length.

parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked the printf call on line 10. The format string uses "%s", which safely prints characters up to the first null terminator and writes to stdout, not the source buffer. Thus no buffer overflow can occur at this sink. Any overflow would have to happen during the allocation or copying of the name string, which is not shown in this fragment. Therefore the reported buffer‑overflow claim at the printf call is unfounded.

finding.title: Integer Overflow
finding.trigger: If the values of int_type->min_value or int_type->max_value exceed the range of the data type used to store them, an integer overflow will occur.
finding.assumptions: The minimum and maximum values are derived from user input or an external source and are not properly validated for range.

parsed.refutation_attempt: The reported untrusted source is the string literal "ConstrainedInt(0->100)" at line 5, which is a compile‑time constant, not input from stdin, argv, network, file, or environment. Since it is hard‑coded, it cannot contain values that overflow an int. Therefore there is no feasible path from an untrusted source to the printf sink. The values 0 and 100 are well within the range of an int, so even if parse_constrained_int_type simply stores them in int fields, no overflow can occur. No additional checks are needed.

finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.trigger: If the source_code contains malicious input that is interpreted as an OS command, it could lead to OS command injection.
finding.assumptions: The parse_constrained_int_type function executes external commands or interprets input in a way that could lead to command execution.

parsed.refutation_attempt: 1) Source of data is a compile‑time constant on line 5, not an untrusted external input such as stdin, argv, a file, or network data. 2) No evidence that parse_constrained_int_type performs any OS command execution is present in the fragment. 3) The code does not call exec, system, popen, or similar functions, and no path from source_code to such a sink exists in the shown snippet.

finding.title: Use After Free
finding.trigger: If int_type is used after it has been freed, a use after free vulnerability could occur.
finding.assumptions: The int_type structure is complex and may contain pointers that are freed but still used later.

parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked that int_type is not accessed after being freed; after line 15 the program terminates and no further dereference occurs. Confirmed that the free calls are in the correct order and no dangling pointer usage follows.
